questions.question: In the sentence, 'Her argument was so convoluted', what is a synonym of the word 'convoluted'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Complex**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"convoluted"** means something that is extremely complex, intricate, or difficult to understand. (जटिल)

 
 
• **Example:** The professor's explanation was so convoluted that even the brightest students struggled to understand.
 
 
 
• **"Complex"** refers to something that is composed of many interconnected parts, making it complicated or intricate. (जटिल)
 
 
• **Example:** The plot of the movie was so complex that it required multiple viewings to fully grasp.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the synonym of **'convoluted'** is **'complex'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Complex**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Straightforward** (सीधा-सादा): Something simple, clear, and easy to understand.

 
 
• **Example:** The instructions were straightforward, so we completed the task without any issues.
 
 
 
• **Neutral** (तटस्थ): Not supporting or favoring any side in a conflict or disagreement.
 
 
• **Example:** The mediator remained neutral during the heated argument between the two parties.
 
 
 
• **Direct** (प्रत्यक्ष): Something that is straight and without deviation.
 
 
• **Example:** She gave a direct answer to the question without any hesitation.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

The proof of the pudding is in the eating

options.text: One has the evidence if they are alert
Trust is built by sharing good food
Its better to be well-fed than to go hungry
A person can only know if something is good or bad by trying it

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"The proof of the pudding is in the eating"** means that the real value or quality of something can only be determined by putting it to the test or experiencing it firsthand. (इसका असली मूल्य या गुणवत्ता केवल इसे आजमाने से पता चल सकता है।)

 
 
• **Example:** He claimed his new recipe was amazing, but the proof of the pudding is in the eating, so I had to taste it to believe him.
 
 
 
• **Explanation of the correct meaning:** The idiom suggests that a person can only know if something is good or bad by trying or experiencing it. (किसी चीज़ की अच्छाई या बुराई को केवल अनुभव करके ही जाना जा सकता है।)
 
 
• **Example:** The new software looks promising, but the proof of the pudding is in the eating; let's use it in real-world scenarios to see how well it works.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1:** One has the evidence if they are alert (यदि वे सतर्क हैं, तो उनके पास सबूत होता है।)

 
 
• **Explanation:** This statement is unrelated to the given idiom.
 
• **Example:** Being alert is important to gather evidence during an investigation.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** Trust is built by sharing good food (भरोसा अच्छे भोजन को साझा करके बनाया जाता है।)
 
 
• **Explanation:** While food can help people bond, this interpretation does not match the idiom.
 
• **Example:** A warm meal can bring people together, but trust goes beyond just sharing food.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** It's better to be well-fed than to go hungry (भूखे रहने से अच्छा है कि भरपेट खाएं।)
 
 
• **Explanation:** This option focuses on hunger and does not explain the idiom's true meaning.
 
• **Example:** It's always wise to plan meals so that no one goes hungry.

questions.question: Identify the sentence with the INCORRECT usage of the adverb.

options.text: The teacher noticed that all students worked laboriously to complete the project on time
The teacher noticed that all students worked strenuous to complete the project on time.
The teacher noticed that all students worked hard to complete the project on time.
The teacher noticed that all students worked meticulously to complete the project on time.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"strenuous"** is an **adjective**, not an adverb. It describes something that requires a lot of effort or energy (e.g., "a strenuous task").
 
• In the sentence, the verb **"worked"** requires an **adverb** to describe how the students worked. Therefore, "strenuous" is grammatically incorrect in this context.
 
• A grammatically correct usage would be: **"worked strenuously."**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Usage:** *"The teacher noticed that all students worked **strenuously**__ to complete the project on time."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "laboriously"** – Correct adverb; means with great effort. (कड़ी मेहनत से)
 
• **Option 3: "hard"** – Correct adverb; irregular form of “hardly.” Means with intensity or diligence. (मेहनत से)
 
• **Option 4: "meticulously"** – Correct adverb; means with great attention to detail. (बारीकी से)

• **Example:** She has been actively involved in community health programs for decades.

• **Example:** She spoke gently to calm the child.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

In the Director’s party,/ everyone noticed/ that he sings more too faster.

options.text: that he sings more too faster

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"more too faster"** is grammatically incorrect because it contains a redundancy.
 
• The word **"faster"** is already a comparative form of "fast" and does not require "more" or "too" before it simultaneously.
 
• You can say either **"too fast"** or **"much faster"**, but **"more too faster"** is incorrect.
 
• The corrected sentence should read: **"that he sings too fast"** or **"that he sings much faster."**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"In the Director’s party, everyone noticed that he sings **too fast**__."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "everyone noticed"** – grammatically correct.
 
• **Option 2: "In the Director’s party,"** – grammatically correct prepositional phrase.
 
• **Option 3: "No error"** – incorrect, as Option 4 clearly contains an error.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The security officer ordered the group ____________ the premises immediately.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**to leave**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"ordered someone to do something"** is the correct grammatical structure used after reporting verbs like "order", "tell", "ask", etc.
 
• Therefore, the verb should be in the infinitive form: **to leave**, not "left", "leaving", or "to left".
 
• This maintains subject-verb agreement and sentence clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"The security officer ordered the group **to leave**__ the premises immediately."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "Left"** is the simple past tense, but it doesn’t follow the correct pattern after "ordered".
 
• **Option 2: "to left"** is grammatically incorrect; "left" cannot follow "to".
 
• **Option 3: "leaving"** is the present participle and does not fit the construction with "ordered".

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Somebody __have left__ dirty clothes on the bed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject **"Somebody"** is a **singular indefinite pronoun**, so it must be followed by a singular verb.
 
• The correct singular verb form of "have" is **"has"**, making the correct phrase: **"Somebody has left"**.
 
• The original sentence incorrectly uses the plural verb "have" with a singular subject.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Somebody **has left**__ dirty clothes on the bed."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "have been left"** – Incorrect as it is passive voice and also mismatches with the singular subject "Somebody".
 
• **Option 3: "was left"** – Incorrect tense and passive voice; also doesn’t match with the plural object "dirty clothes".
 
• **Option 4: "were left"** – Also passive and does not match with the singular subject "Somebody".

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

3D printing is an exciting new technology _______ promises to very quickly create anything people can design.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**that**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"that"** is a relative pronoun used to introduce a defining clause, giving essential information about the noun it follows — in this case, "technology."
 
• The clause "**that promises to very quickly create anything people can design**" describes the function of 3D printing.
 
• Thus, "that" correctly connects the noun "technology" with the action it performs.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"3D printing is an exciting new technology **that**__ promises to very quickly create anything people can design."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "the"** – Incorrect article; does not connect clauses.
 
• **Option 2: "then"** – An adverb used for sequencing, not for introducing a relative clause.
 
• **Option 3: "than"** – Used in comparisons, not appropriate here.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Brutal
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Ruthless**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Brutal"** means harsh, cruel, or extremely violent. It is used to describe actions or behavior lacking compassion or mercy. (क्रूर)

 
 
• **Example:** The dictator's brutal policies led to widespread suffering among the people.
 
 
 
• **"Ruthless"** refers to showing no pity or compassion for others. It is synonymous with "Brutal" as both imply a lack of mercy or kindness. (निर्दयी)
 
 
• **Example:** The ruthless leader crushed any opposition to his rule without hesitation.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the synonym of **"Brutal"** is **"Ruthless"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Ruthless**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Active** (सक्रिय): Energetic or involved in action.

 
 
• **Example:** She is very active in community service and volunteers regularly.
